summary: Period-5 tape; 5-state walls drift right x1.5 per level (3/2 conveyor); right-edge counter absorbs them; no halt branch.
mechanism: Tape = period-5 pattern: B sweeping right turns 11000 into 10111; C sweeping left turns it back (5 steps/block).
Walls are 5-state gadgets: B bounces once then passes, C twice then passes; each round moves a wall 5 cells right.
So each wall is crossed 3/2 as often as the one to its left; walls are born at the left, absorbed at the right.

template.note: Template compares two unary counters (x -> 2x-1, sigma_score_unbounded_nonhalt). From its S1/Inc_a configs our machine hits 0/60 targets and halts 25/60; only its Inductive trip relation P is reusable.

strategy: Prove sweeps with ind and the 5 wall rules with es. Encode the tape as a list of (segment length, wall state) with an Inductive trip relation (CounterCmp_v1 P, BECv7 digit encoding); prove one head trip by induction on the list, then a closed invariant (left gadget + list + right barrier) and finish with progress_nonhalt_cond / multistep_nonhalt.
risks: Right barrier (0001 zone) is a second counter: last-segment growth per cycle is 4-12 blocks depending on a; needs its own case analysis.
Exact wall spacings follow a 3/2 rounding orbit; the invariant must bound them, not pin them (200/200 perturbed tapes ran 1e8 steps without halting).
No proof in this class yet; nested trip induction may give a 30-60 KB file.
